planningWindow: Target around September 3-16, 2026, flexible by 1-2 days
notes: Flight pricing and exact hotel availability still need a departure airport and live booking pass.
Budget ranges are planning placeholders for two adults and one lap/seat-flexible one-year-old, excluding unusually expensive business-class flights.
For baby-friendly planning, prefer two- or three-base itineraries, short hikes, kitchens/laundry where possible, and one or two memorable splurge nights rather than luxury every night.

trips.name: Austria + Alpine Borders
trips.route: Munich or Zurich · Tyrol · Lech/Arlberg · Bavaria or Appenzell
trips.babyPacing: Best with 3 bases and trains/short drives
trips.summary: The strongest match for alpine farms, cowbells, polished wellness, mountain lifts, and cozy food culture without repeating Zermatt/Interlaken.
trips.editorialNote: Best version: focus Austria/Tyrol + Bavaria or eastern Switzerland. True western Switzerland adds distance and may dilute the relaxed family pace.
bestFor: Farm animals, alpine meadow walks, cable cars, and stroller/carrier-friendly mountain towns.
A one-night or two-night splurge at a true farm-and-spa resort.
Recreating the emotional tone of Switzerland while seeing new terrain.
watchouts: Can become too many countries unless the route is kept disciplined.
High-end family rooms at the best resorts can push the full trip above $10k.
Car seats, luggage, and train transfers need careful choreography.

trips.name: Banff + Lake Louise
trips.route: Calgary · Canmore/Banff · Lake Louise · Icefields Parkway
trips.september: Great weather window; popular but easing
trips.babyPacing: High if based in Canmore/Banff plus 2-3 Lake Louise nights
trips.summary: A visually spectacular, relatively straightforward mountain trip with excellent stroller-friendly walks, lakefront splurge options, and easy road-trip logistics.
trips.editorialNote: This is probably the easiest North American version of the Switzerland feeling, but it is less farmstead-forward than Austria or Iceland.
bestFor: Lake Louise Lakeshore, Bow River Pathway, Johnston Canyon, gondolas, and scenic drives.
A lower-friction international trip with a baby.
One polished spa/lakefront stay surrounded by simpler condo nights.
watchouts: Lake Louise and Moraine Lake lodging can be extremely expensive.
Moraine Lake access requires shuttle planning; private cars are restricted.
Farm-to-table exists, but the trip is more national-park lodge than farmstay.

trips.name: Iceland Farm + South Coast
trips.route: Reykjavik · Golden Circle farm stay · South Coast · Snæfellsnes optional
trips.babyPacing: High if self-drive route stays compact
trips.summary: The best farmstay candidate outside the Alps: cows, horses, geothermal pools, waterfalls, short walks, and huge landscapes without needing long hikes.
trips.editorialNote: Blue Lagoon is not suitable for a one-year-old in the water because the minimum age is two; Secret Lagoon and local pools are better planning targets.
bestFor: Farm-to-table meals with animals directly integrated into the stay.
Short scenic stops that work around naps: waterfalls, black beaches, horses, geothermal areas.
A trip that feels different from Switzerland while still nature-first.
watchouts: Weather can be windy and wet; every day needs a backup plan.
The Ring Road is too much with a one-year-old in 12-14 days unless you want lots of driving.
Some famous spas have child age limits.

trips.name: Scotland Highlands
trips.route: Edinburgh · Perthshire/Trossachs · Cairngorms · Skye or west coast
trips.summary: A gentler cultural/nature blend: Highland animals, lochs, castles, farm hotels, dramatic drives, and excellent food if the itinerary avoids too much road time.
trips.editorialNote: This may be the best non-Alps emotional trip: less vertical hiking, more storybook villages, farm tours, estate activities, and cozy downtime.
bestFor: Farm tours, Highland cows, lochside hotels, castles, gentle walks, and moody scenery.
A few nights at a grand resort or food-focused farm hotel.
Pairing outdoors with indoor backup plans.
watchouts: Skye and west coast routes can involve long drives with a baby.
Weather is a real part of the trip; waterproof gear matters.
Some luxury hotels are more adult-artful than toddler-practical.

trips.name: Grand Teton + Jackson Hole
trips.route: Jackson · Grand Teton · optional Yellowstone edge
trips.summary: A beautiful, simpler domestic mountain trip with iconic views, lakeside walks, cabins, wildlife, and easier logistics than Alaska.
trips.editorialNote: This is strong for scenery and ease, weaker for farm-to-table/farmstay unless paired with Jackson-area ranch stays or one big splurge.
bestFor: Short hikes like Taggart Lake, lakeshore walks, Jenny Lake boat, wildlife drives.
A domestic trip with less passport and time-zone complexity.
Cabins and kitchenettes that make baby logistics easier.
watchouts: Jackson Hole lodging can be expensive for what you get.
September can bring chilly mornings and early snow at elevation.
Yellowstone add-on increases drive time quickly.

trips.name: Alaska Kenai + Anchorage
trips.september: Early Sept can work; services start tapering
trips.summary: The biggest adventure candidate: glaciers, wildlife, coastal scenery, and lodges. It can be unforgettable, but it needs the most caution with weather, drive times, and baby comfort.
trips.editorialNote: Best as an Anchorage/Seward/Girdwood trip rather than trying to do Denali, Kenai, and remote lodges all at once.
bestFor: Glaciers, wildlife centers, easy coastal walks, scenic train segments, and dramatic landscapes.
A once-in-a-while adventure if you are comfortable with weather variability.
One remote or semi-remote lodge splurge if budget allows.
watchouts: Boat tours may be rough or too long with a one-year-old.
Luxury lodges can blow the budget quickly.
Some seasonal operations close around mid-September.

trips.name: Newfoundland Coast + Gros Morne
trips.vibe: Atlantic villages and wild fjord coast
trips.route: St. John's · Trinity/Bonavista · Twillingate · Fogo Island · Gros Morne
trips.september: Strong shoulder-season fit, with weather and boat flexibility needed
trips.babyPacing: Medium-High if drives are broken and boat days stay optional
trips.summary: A distinctive Atlantic Canada trip with colorful St. John's, puffins/lighthouses, fishing villages, Fogo Island design-and-coast splurge potential, and a Gros Morne mountain-and-fjord finale.
trips.editorialNote: Best version flies open-jaw into St. John's and home from Deer Lake. Fogo Island Inn is a special upgrade, not the baseline stay, because it can overwhelm the budget.
bestFor: A place that feels culturally and visually different from the Alps/Rockies while staying nature-first.
Short coastal walks, lighthouses, village food, puffin/whale options, and dramatic Gros Morne scenery.
A controlled Fogo Island splurge without making the whole trip luxury-priced.
watchouts: Boat tours and ferries need weather-flexible planning with a one-year-old.
Distances across Newfoundland are real; Fogo plus Gros Morne creates one long transfer day.
Puffin sightings are seasonal and may be late by early September.
